aisles.decision: Choose organic meat and eggs with pasture-raising certification, checking grass-fed wording on organ meats.
Choose wild seafood with a species label, live shellfish with closing shells, and dry scallops.
Choose plain whole cultured dairy with milk and cultures listed, and cream without additives.
Choose sealed organic foods with grain, nut, sweetener or oil named, and stated BPA-free can linings.
Choose organic sourdough or sprouted bread with whole grain named first, without enriched flour.
Read snack ingredients for named foods and oils, skipping natural flavors and added syrups.
Choose organic condiments listing vegetables, vinegar, salt, spices and any oil by name.
Choose plain water or organic kombucha in glass, checking for added sugar or natural flavors.

picks.decision: Grass-fed, grass-finished beef jerky with simple ingredients.
picks.avoid: First ingredient beef; AGA or organic seal on the bag.

picks.title: Venison
picks.decision: Venison in a tray naming deer.
picks.avoid: Tray names deer and shows an inspected and approved mark.

picks.title: Flavored yogurt
picks.decision: Skip sweetened or flavored yogurt; choose plain whole yogurt.
picks.avoid: Skip yogurt listing organic sweeteners or “natural flavors”.

picks.title: Dairy cream
picks.decision: Organic dairy cream with cream as the only ingredient.
picks.avoid: Check cream alone in ingredients; skip cartons stamped “ultra-pasteurized”.

picks.title: Non-dairy creamer
picks.decision: Skip non-dairy creamer; choose plain dairy cream.
picks.avoid: Skip creamer listing oil or sweeteners before any dairy ingredient.

picks.title: Cheese food slices
picks.decision: Skip cheese food slices; choose slices labeled cheese.
picks.avoid: “Pasteurized process cheese food” or “cheese product” printed on the wrapper.

picks.decision: Skip margarine; choose butter with cream and salt.
picks.avoid: “Vegetable oil” leads the ingredient list of any tub or stick.

picks.decision: Skip imitation whipped topping; choose plain cream to whip.
picks.avoid: “Hydrogenated” or vegetable oil on a canned or tub topping.

picks.title: Vegetable oil blend
picks.decision: Skip vegetable oil blends; choose a single named olive oil.
picks.avoid: Bottle reads “vegetable oil” or lists soybean, canola, corn, cottonseed.

picks.title: Avocado oil
picks.decision: Organic virgin avocado oil with a harvest or production date.
picks.avoid: Check harvest or production date; choose “virgin”, not “refined”.

picks.title: Whole grains
picks.decision: Organic whole grains with one grain named in the ingredients.
picks.avoid: Ingredient list is one grain, with “whole” before its name.

picks.title: Dried pulses
picks.decision: Organic dried lentils or split peas with one legume listed.
picks.avoid: One legume named; soak-and-cook directions printed on the bag.

picks.title: Dry pasta
picks.decision: Organic whole-wheat pasta with semolina named and no enriched flour.
picks.avoid: Read durum or whole-wheat semolina; skip “enriched” in the pasta ingredients.

picks.title: Molasses
picks.decision: Organic molasses with molasses listed before other sweeteners.
picks.avoid: Read molasses or dehydrated cane juice first, before other sweeteners.

picks.title: Date and coconut sugar
picks.decision: Organic date or coconut sweeteners named by their plant.
picks.avoid: Read the sweetener’s plant name, not “natural sweetener”, in ingredients.

picks.title: Refined syrups
picks.decision: Skip corn, agave and brown rice syrups; choose pure maple syrup.
picks.avoid: Corn syrup, agave or brown rice syrup anywhere in the ingredients.

picks.title: Nuts and seeds
picks.decision: Organic raw nuts and seeds in sealed packages.
picks.avoid: Check sealed packaging and nuts alone in ingredients; skip open bins.

picks.title: Canned vegetables and fish
picks.decision: Organic canned foods with stated BPA-free lining and simple ingredients.
picks.avoid: Label states BPA-free lining; ingredients are the food, water, salt.

picks.title: Jarred vegetable sauces
picks.decision: Organic jarred vegetable sauces with named oil, salt and spices.
picks.avoid: Glass jar; vegetables, oil by name, salt and spices, nothing else.

picks.title: Soy sauce
picks.decision: Organic naturally fermented or brewed soy sauce.
picks.avoid: Read naturally fermented or brewed; skip liquid amino acids.

picks.decision: Skip juice and juice cocktails; choose plain water.
picks.avoid: Read “from concentrate” or “juice cocktail”; check for listed sweeteners.

picks.decision: Skip soda; choose plain water without flavors or sweeteners.
picks.avoid: Skip soda listing sweeteners, caramel color or “natural flavors”.

picks.title: Breakfast cereal
picks.decision: Skip extruded breakfast cereal; choose organic whole-grain hot cereal.
picks.avoid: Skip extruded rings, flakes, puffs, or cereal boxes marked “natural”.

picks.decision: Organic grass-finished marrow bones with an AGA label at the counter.
picks.avoid: Read grass-finished or AGA on marrow bones at the counter.

picks.decision: Organic sausage with a third-party welfare seal for outdoor access.
picks.avoid: Check short casing ingredients and a welfare seal for outdoor access.

picks.decision: Wild pollock fish sticks made from fillet, not minced pieces.
picks.avoid: Read wild pollock fillet; skip fish sticks made from minced pieces.

organ_meats.decision: Organic organ meats from pasture-raised animals.
organ_meats.why: Weston A. Price says sourcing is key for organ meats and points to pasture-raised, 100% grass-fed animals.

beef_veal.decision: Pasture-raised veal with a humane seal.
beef_veal.why: Pasture-raised veal means calves raised on open pasture beside the mother, never in feedlots.
beef_veal.instead: Pasture-raised veal with a humane seal.

chicken_breast.decision: Organic, pasture-raised chicken breast, bone-in and skin-on.
chicken_breast.why: Certified Humane pasture raised requires 108 square feet per bird outdoors, matching AWA.

bacon.decision: Pasture-raised bacon with pork, salt and celery powder.
bacon.why: The USDA rule lets “Uncured” appear in the name only for products cured without synthetic nitrite.

ham.decision: Uncured whole-muscle ham with pork and salt.
ham.why: “Uncured” must lead the product name under federal curing rules.
ham.tier_note: Uncured is regulated wording at the start of the product name, not a pasture certification.

turkey_bacon.decision: Uncured turkey bacon with turkey listed first.
turkey_bacon.why: 9 CFR 317.17 requires the term Uncured before the product name on products cured without nitrite.

cured_pork.decision: Dry-cured pork with pork and salt only.
cured_pork.why: “Uncured” wording is regulated product-name text for cured meats.

deli_meat_uncured.decision: Uncured deli meat sliced from a whole roast.
deli_meat_uncured.why: The word “Uncured” must precede the product name on cured-style meats.

egg_labels.decision: Organic eggs with a Certified Humane Pasture Raised seal.
egg_labels.why: Pasture raised under Certified Humane means 108 square feet per hen versus 2 for free range.

label_cage_free.decision: Pasture-raised eggs with an outdoor-access certification.
label_cage_free.why: Certified Humane free range needs 2 square feet outdoors; cage-free carries no outdoor figure.
label_cage_free.instead: Pasture-raised eggs with an outdoor-access certification.

label_pasture_raised_feed.decision: Organic pasture-raised eggs with Certified Humane or AWA certification.
label_pasture_raised_feed.why: Certified Humane and AWA pasture-raised standards both specify 108 square feet per bird.

egg_duck_quail.decision: Pastured duck eggs in a carton naming duck.
egg_duck_quail.why: The Weston A. Price shopping guide lists pastured duck eggs among its best eggs.

seafood_certifications.decision: Wild seafood with the MSC fish checkmark and chain-of-custody code.
seafood_certifications.why: The MSC mark is only for wild fish from certified fisheries.

canned_tuna.decision: Pole-caught, troll-caught, FAD-free or school-caught canned tuna.
canned_tuna.why: Seafood Watch points to canned tuna with pole-caught, troll-caught, FAD-free, free school or school-caught on the label.

canned_fish_choosing.decision: Wild canned sardines with skin and bones in olive oil.
canned_fish_choosing.why: Weston A. Price recommends sardines with skin and bones as high in vitamin D and a good source of calcium.

mercury_by_fish.decision: Choose sardines with the fish named on the can.
mercury_by_fish.why: A Weston A. Price article lists sardines among a short list of recommended fish for low mercury.

seafood_fish_roe.decision: Salmon roe with only roe and salt.
seafood_fish_roe.why: Weston A. Price calls roe a rich source of vitamins A and D, very long-chain fatty acids, and zinc.

scallops.decision: Dry-packed scallops without milky liquid in the tray.
scallops.why: Dry scallops have not been soaked in sodium tripolyphosphate.

crab.why: Foodal advises choosing live crabs that are active and moving, and heavy in the hand.

clams_mussels_oysters.decision: Live shellfish with closed shells and a harvest tag.
clams_mussels_oysters.why: Pacific Coast Shellfish Growers say oysters should always be tightly closed and mussels should close when tapped.

yogurt_plain_vs_flavored.decision: Organic plain whole yogurt with milk and named cultures.
yogurt_plain_vs_flavored.why: Cornucopia notes certified organic yogurt can still carry a high amount of sugar. Plain organic tubs let the shopper add fruit; WAPF rates plain, whole yogurt as good.

plain_kefir.decision: Organic whole-milk kefir with milk and cultures only.
plain_kefir.why: WAPF rates plain, whole yogurt and kefir without added vitamins, preferably grass-fed, as good.

sour_cream.decision: Organic sour cream with cream and cultures only.
sour_cream.why: WAPF lists sour cream with additives, and homogenized cream, under avoid.

grassfed_butter.decision: Organic butter with cream and salt, without natural flavors.
grassfed_butter.why: WAPF rates pasteurized butter without natural flavors, preferably grass-fed, as good.
grassfed_butter.tier_note: Butter’s ingredient list shows whether the cream and salt have added natural flavors.

ghee.decision: Organic ghee with butterfat or clarified butter alone.
ghee.why: WAPF rates pasteurized ghee without natural flavors, preferably grass-fed, as good.

cheese_real_vs_processed.decision: Organic cheese labeled cheese, without cheese-food or cheese-product wording.
cheese_real_vs_processed.why: Pasteurized process cheese is cheeses ground and mixed with heat, a different standard of identity than the cheese itself.

cream_cheese.decision: Organic cream cheese without gums or added thickeners.
cream_cheese.why: WAPF lists lowfat and fat-free cream cheese, and cream cheese made with additives, under avoid.

cottage_cheese.decision: Organic cottage cheese with named cultures and no gums.
cottage_cheese.why: WAPF lists lowfat and fat-free cottage cheese, and cottage cheese made with additives, under avoid.

ice_cream.decision: Organic vanilla ice cream with cream, milk and egg yolks.
ice_cream.why: WAPF rates simple flavors made with milk, cream, egg yolks and real vanilla as good. It avoids extenders and natural flavors.

canned_coconut_milk.decision: Organic canned coconut milk with coconut and water only.
canned_coconut_milk.why: WAPF recommends canned whole coconut milk without additives, preferably in BPA-free containers.

plant_butter.decision: Butter with cream and salt instead of vegetable-oil spreads.
plant_butter.why: WAPF avoid list covers spreads combining butter with vegetable oils and most commercial vegetable and seed oils.
plant_butter.instead: Butter with cream and salt instead of vegetable-oil spreads.

cooking_oils.decision: Organic cooking oil naming olive, coconut or avocado alone.
cooking_oils.why: WAPF avoids most commercial vegetable and seed oils. It lists extra virgin olive oil and avocado oil among good fats, favoring a single named oil.

olive_oil_grades.decision: Organic extra-virgin olive oil with a harvest date.
olive_oil_grades.why: UC Davis says dark glass, metal tins and bag-in-box protect oil from light. A harvest date shows freshness; WAPF lists extra virgin olive oil among good fats.

label_cold_pressed_expeller.decision: Organic oil labeled cold pressed or expeller pressed.
label_cold_pressed_expeller.why: Organic handling rules bar volatile synthetic solvents as processing aids.

lard_tallow.decision: Organic lard or tallow with pasture or grass-fed wording.
lard_tallow.why: WAPF rates lard from pigs raised outdoors and tallow from grass-fed cows and sheep as best fats.

rancidity_check.decision: Organic oil in dark glass or tin, without a stale-nut smell.
rancidity_check.why: UC Davis names stale nuts as a smell of rancid oil and clear plastic as least protective.

rice_arsenic.decision: Organic whole-grain rice with rice as the only ingredient.
rice_arsenic.why: WAPF rates organic whole grain rice among the best grains and lists white rice under avoid.

grains_beyond_rice.decision: Organic quinoa, millet or buckwheat with one grain listed.
grains_beyond_rice.why: WAPF lists all non-organic grains and legumes under avoid; MSU Extension lists millet as a whole grain.

wild_rice.decision: Organic wild rice with no white-rice blend.
wild_rice.why: WAPF rates wildcrafted wild rice as best and lists white rice under avoid. MSU Extension lists wild rice as a whole grain.

beans_dried_vs_canned.decision: Organic dried beans first, canned beans with stated BPA-free lining next.
beans_dried_vs_canned.why: WAPF rates organic dried beans as best and organic canned legumes as good, eaten only once or twice a month.

specialty_flours.decision: Organic alternative flours with one flour named.
specialty_flours.why: WAPF rates freshly ground, soaked organic whole grain flours as best and organic sprouted flours as good.

label_multigrain_vs_whole_grain.decision: Organic grains labeled whole grain, beyond multigrain wording.
label_multigrain_vs_whole_grain.why: MSU Extension says multigrain is a mixture of grains, possibly all or mostly refined. The Whole Grains Council also says it may describe refined grains.

sprouted_grain_bread.decision: Organic sprouted-grain bread with sprouted grains named first.
sprouted_grain_bread.why: WAPF rates sourdough, soaked or sprouted breads from freshly ground organic whole grain flour as best.

sandwich_bread.decision: Organic sourdough or sprouted whole-grain sandwich bread.
sandwich_bread.why: WAPF lists most commercial breads, based on white flour with hydrogenated oils, added gluten, soy or additives, under avoid.
sandwich_bread.instead: Organic sourdough or sprouted whole-grain sandwich bread.

gluten_free_bread.decision: Gluten-free bread with a named whole-grain flour first.
gluten_free_bread.why: The Whole Grains Council says a first ingredient containing “whole” likely means a mostly whole-grain product. That wording is not a guarantee.
gluten_free_bread.instead: Gluten-free bread with a named whole-grain flour first.

bagels.decision: Organic sourdough or sprouted bagels without ascorbic acid.
bagels.why: WAPF rates sourdough, soaked or sprouted breads from organic whole grain flour as best. It lists breads containing ascorbic acid under avoid.
bagels.instead: Organic sourdough or sprouted bagels without ascorbic acid.

sugars.decision: Organic cane sugar named as dehydrated cane juice.
sugars.why: WAPF lists dehydrated sugar cane juice among best sweeteners and white sugar under avoid.

maple_syrup.decision: Organic pure maple syrup with no corn syrup.
maple_syrup.why: WAPF lists maple syrup as a best sweetener and imitation syrups under avoid.

nuts_raw_vs_roasted.decision: Organic raw nuts in sealed packs without sugar or coatings.
nuts_raw_vs_roasted.why: WAPF rates fresh organic raw nuts in sealed packages as best. It lists nut mixtures with sugar, agave or flavorings under avoid.

nut_butter_ingredients.decision: Organic nut butter with nuts and optional salt only.
nut_butter_ingredients.why: WAPF avoid list covers nut butters with hydrogenated oils, sugar, agave or flavorings.

seeds.decision: Organic raw seeds with one seed named in a sealed pack.
seeds.why: WAPF rates fresh organic raw seeds in sealed packages as best.

trail_mix.decision: Organic plain nuts instead of sweetened or oil-coated trail mix.
trail_mix.why: WAPF avoid list names nut mixtures with partially hydrogenated oils, sugar, chocolate or flavorings.
trail_mix.instead: Organic plain nuts instead of sweetened or oil-coated trail mix.

pasta_sauce.decision: Organic pasta sauce with tomatoes first and no added sugar.
pasta_sauce.why: WAPF lists most commercial sauces, ketchup and other condiments under avoid.

seaweed.decision: Organic sea vegetables with a named species and origin outside China.
seaweed.why: WAPF rates whole or powdered sea vegetables not from China as best. It lists seaweed from China, even organic, under avoid.

hummus.decision: Organic hummus with chickpeas, tahini and olive oil.
hummus.why: WAPF avoid list names canola and soy oils.

dried_herbs.decision: Organic single-herb jars without citric acid or MSG.
dried_herbs.why: WAPF avoid list covers spices and blends containing MSG, citric acid or hydrolyzed protein.

whole_spices.decision: Organic whole spices with one seed or stick named.
whole_spices.why: WAPF lists spices and blends containing MSG, citric acid, hydrolyzed protein or other additives under avoid.

salt.decision: Unrefined gray, pink, red or beige salt without iodized wording.
salt.why: WAPF lists unrefined salt in light gray, pink, red or beige as best and iodized salt as avoid.

baking_powder.decision: Aluminum-free baking powder in a labeled tin.
baking_powder.why: WAPF lists aluminum-free baking powder as best and baking powder containing aluminum under avoid.

raw_cider_vinegar.decision: Organic raw, unfiltered apple cider vinegar with visible mother.
raw_cider_vinegar.why: WAPF lists organic raw vinegars as best.

vinegar.decision: Apple cider, wine or balsamic vinegar instead of distilled white vinegar.
vinegar.why: WAPF avoid list names distilled vinegar.
vinegar.instead: Apple cider, wine or balsamic vinegar instead of distilled white vinegar.

ketchup_mustard.decision: Organic mustard or fermented ketchup without natural flavors.
ketchup_mustard.why: WAPF lists organic mustard and organic fermented ketchup among best condiments.

condiments.decision: Mayonnaise or dressings with olive oil instead of soy or canola.
condiments.why: WAPF avoid list names soy and canola oils.
condiments.instead: Mayonnaise or dressings with olive oil instead of soy or canola.

crackers.decision: Organic whole-grain crackers without hydrogenated oil or soy flour.
crackers.why: WAPF lists most commercial crackers based on white flour with partially hydrogenated oils, soy flour or additives under avoid.
crackers.instead: Organic whole-grain crackers without hydrogenated oil or soy flour.

pretzels.decision: Whole-grain pretzels with whole flour listed first.
pretzels.why: WAPF lists white flour products under avoid.
pretzels.instead: Whole-grain pretzels with whole flour listed first.

rice_cakes_puffed_grains.decision: Organic whole-grain crackers instead of puffed rice cakes.
rice_cakes_puffed_grains.why: WAPF lists puffed grain products such as rice cakes under avoid.
rice_cakes_puffed_grains.instead: Organic whole-grain crackers instead of puffed rice cakes.

bottled_water_buying.decision: Bottled spring water with spring water printed on the label.
bottled_water_buying.why: Spring water must come from the spring or a bore hole tapping the underground formation feeding it.

kombucha.decision: Organic kombucha with black tea in a glass bottle.
kombucha.why: WAPF recommends organic lacto-fermented beverages in glass jars, such as kombucha made with organic black tea.

coconut_water.decision: Organic coconut water with coconut water alone, outside aseptic boxes.
coconut_water.why: WAPF lists coconut products in aseptic boxes under avoid.
coconut_water.tier_note: The coconut water ingredient list and aseptic packaging are visible product checks.

beef_grassfed_vs_grainfed.decision: Organic grass-finished beef with the AGA Grassfed seal.
beef_grassfed_vs_grainfed.why: AGA animals eat only grass and forage from weaning until harvest, on pasture, never given antibiotics.

beef_cuts_basics.decision: Organic whole beef cuts in sealed trays with AGA Grassfed certification.
beef_cuts_basics.why: Whole cuts keep the meat intact; the organic seal identifies a certified organic feed ration, including pasture and forage.

ground_beef_lean_ratio.decision: Organic grass-finished ground beef with its lean ratio printed.
ground_beef_lean_ratio.why: Grass-finished wording identifies the feeding choice; organic rules exclude meat from animals treated with antibiotics.

hot_dogs.decision: Grass-fed beef hot dogs with an AGA seal and short ingredient list.
hot_dogs.why: AGA animals are fed only grass and forage and never given added growth hormones.

lamb_goat.decision: Organic lamb or goat with an AWA pasture seal.
lamb_goat.why: AWA guarantees animals live outdoors on pasture or range for their entire lives.

bison.decision: Organic bison with the AGA Grassfed mark and bison alone listed.
bison.why: AGA requires a 100% grass diet from weaning until harvest.

chicken_cuts_basics.decision: Organic whole chicken with an AWA seal and no basting solution.
chicken_cuts_basics.why: AWA guarantees outdoor pasture life for the whole animal.

poultry_chicken_wings.decision: Organic pasture-raised chicken wings with intact skin and no coating.
poultry_chicken_wings.why: Plain skin-on wings keep the cut intact; organic livestock rules require certified organic feed.

rotisserie_chicken.decision: Rotisserie chicken listing only chicken and salt.
rotisserie_chicken.why: Chicken and salt keep the recipe simple; the organic seal identifies certified organic livestock feed.

turkey_whole.decision: Organic whole turkey with pasture-raising certification.
turkey_whole.why: An unbasted whole bird avoids added basting solution; organic rules require certified organic feed.

ground_turkey.decision: Organic ground turkey listing breast and thigh meat only.
ground_turkey.why: Breast and thigh alone identify the meat in the pack; antibiotic-treated birds cannot be sold as organic.

poultry_duck.decision: Organic whole duck with skin on and an AWA seal.
poultry_duck.why: AWA covers duck standards and requires pasture or range living.

pork_cuts_and_enhanced.decision: Organic pasture-raised pork chops without added solution.
pork_cuts_and_enhanced.why: AWA guarantees pigs live outdoors on pasture or range.

salmon_wild_vs_farmed.decision: Wild Alaskan salmon with the species named and sockeye flesh deep red.
salmon_wild_vs_farmed.why: Wild is the seafood premise; the wild or farm-raised label identifies the production method.

label_wild_vs_farm_raised.decision: Wild fish with country and catch method named on the tag.
label_wild_vs_farm_raised.why: Wild is the seafood premise; the production-method label distinguishes wild from farm-raised fish.

farmed_fish_by_species.decision: Farmed fish carrying the ASC logo on the pack.
farmed_fish_by_species.why: ASC says seafood carrying its label on pack was farmed with care.

shrimp_imported_vs_domestic.decision: Wild Gulf or US shrimp, shell on, without additives.
shrimp_imported_vs_domestic.why: Shell-on shrimp without additives keep the product close to the catch; wild or farm-raised wording identifies its production method.

white_fish.decision: Wild Pacific cod with species named and gray-brown skin visible.
white_fish.why: Pacific cod have gray or brown skin with a paler belly; skin left on provides a visible species check.

seafood_fresh_sardines_mackerel.decision: Fresh wild sardines with shiny skin or mackerel with vivid stripes.
seafood_fresh_sardines_mackerel.why: Mackerel color fades quickly after death, so dull stripes signal age.

lobster.decision: Live lobster with moving claws, or hard-frozen tails without ice glaze.
lobster.why: American lobster is primarily sold live or frozen; those are the two forms to check at the counter.

smoked_salmon.decision: Chilled smoked salmon with origin and wild or farm-raised wording.
smoked_salmon.why: Wild or farm-raised wording identifies the fish production method when provided; it does not describe the smoking process.

seafood_counter.decision: Whole fish on ice with clear eyes and a species sign.
seafood_counter.why: Whole fish on ice should look bright-eyed with shiny skin, as the sardine guidance describes.

whole_vs_reduced_fat_milk.decision: Organic whole milk without ultra-pasteurized wording near the date.
whole_vs_reduced_fat_milk.why: Whole milk keeps its milkfat, and WAPF lists ultra-pasteurized milk products under avoid. Ultra-pasteurized describes a heat-processing method.

oats_steelcut_rolled_instant.decision: Organic whole-grain oats without flavorings or added sugar.
oats_steelcut_rolled_instant.why: Whole oats without flavor or sugar keep the ingredient list to the grain. Organic rules bar excluded methods; WAPF describes soaking, sprouting or fermenting grains.

cornmeal_polenta_grits.decision: Organic whole-grain cornmeal or grits without degerminated wording.
cornmeal_polenta_grits.why: Corn is on the Non-GMO Project High-Risk List. The Whole Grains Council says degerminated cornmeal never describes a whole grain.

flour_basics.decision: Organic whole-wheat flour without bleached or enriched wording.
flour_basics.why: WAPF says avoid white flour and white flour products, and lists bleached white flour under avoid.

sourdough.why: WAPF rates sourdough bread from organic whole grain flour as best and says genuine sourdough fermentation breaks down gluten.

honey_adulteration.decision: Organic raw, unfiltered honey with pollen left in the jar.
honey_adulteration.why: WAPF lists raw honey, preferably unfiltered, among its best sweeteners; ultra-filtration removes pollen.

snack_bars.decision: Whole nuts or fruit instead of bars with syrups or soy protein isolate.
snack_bars.why: WAPF lists brown rice syrup and agave under avoid; whole nuts or fruit keep the snack ingredients recognizable.
snack_bars.instead: Whole nuts or fruit instead of bars with syrups or soy protein isolate.

snacks.decision: Organic potato or corn chips with olive or coconut oil and salt.
snacks.why: WAPF lists most commercial vegetable and seed oils under avoid and olive and organic virgin coconut oil among best.
snacks.tier_note: Potato flour and vegetable powder are visible ingredient checks for veggie chips.

do_lines.organ_meats: Liver or heart pack carrying an organic or AGA seal.
do_lines.beef_veal: Only if label says pasture-raised with a humane seal.
do_lines.chicken_breast: Bone-in, skin-on breast with USDA Organic plus Certified Humane Pasture Raised.
do_lines.bacon: Ingredients show pork, salt, celery powder only; pasture seal on pack.
do_lines.ham: Whole-muscle ham whose name begins Uncured, ingredients listing salt and pork.
do_lines.turkey_bacon: Name reads Uncured turkey bacon; turkey listed first.
do_lines.cured_pork: Dry-cured wording on pack; ingredient list is pork and salt.
do_lines.deli_meat_uncured: Uncured on the deli label; whole roast sliced fresh.
do_lines.egg_labels: Carton shows USDA Organic and Certified Humane Pasture Raised.
do_lines.label_cage_free: Cage-free only on carton, no outdoor access seal.
do_lines.label_pasture_raised_feed: Certified Humane or AWA Pasture Raised plus USDA Organic seal.
do_lines.egg_duck_quail: Carton names duck and says pastured.
do_lines.seafood_certifications: Blue MSC fish checkmark with a chain-of-custody code.
do_lines.canned_tuna: Label says pole-caught, troll-caught, FAD-free or school-caught.
do_lines.canned_fish_choosing: Sardines labeled skin and bones, wild-caught, in olive oil.
do_lines.seafood_fish_roe: Jar lists salmon roe and salt only.
do_lines.scallops: Dry-packed scallops sitting without milky liquid in the tray.
do_lines.clams_mussels_oysters: Shells close when tapped; harvest tag on the bag.
do_lines.yogurt_plain_vs_flavored: Ingredient list reads milk and named cultures, with no sugar, pectin or flavors.
do_lines.plain_kefir: Whole milk kefir; ingredients are milk and kefir cultures.
do_lines.sour_cream: Ingredients: cream and cultures; no starch, gums or flavor words.
do_lines.grassfed_butter: Ingredients: cream, salt; skip any “natural flavor” entry.
do_lines.ghee: Ingredient reads butterfat or clarified butter alone; no oil blended in.
do_lines.cheese_real_vs_processed: Name reads “cheese”, never “cheese food” or “cheese product”.
do_lines.cream_cheese: Ingredients: cream, milk, salt, cultures; no gums or added thickeners.
do_lines.cottage_cheese: Cultures named; carrageenan or gums not in the ingredient list.
do_lines.ice_cream: Cream, milk, egg yolks and real vanilla; no “flavor” words or extenders.
do_lines.canned_coconut_milk: Can with coconut and water only; BPA-free lining stated.
do_lines.plant_butter: Palm, canola or “vegetable oil blend” in the ingredient list.
do_lines.cooking_oils: One oil named on the label: olive, coconut or avocado, not a blend.
do_lines.olive_oil_grades: Harvest date printed, dark glass or tin, “extra virgin” on the front.
do_lines.label_cold_pressed_expeller: “Cold pressed” or “expeller pressed” printed on the front of the bottle.
do_lines.lard_tallow: Lard or tallow the only ingredient; “pastured” or “grass-fed” on the label.
do_lines.rancidity_check: Check oil for stale-nut smells on opening; skip clear plastic bottles.
do_lines.rice_arsenic: Rice the only ingredient; brown rice syrup is a separate skip.
do_lines.grains_beyond_rice: Quinoa, millet or buckwheat the only ingredient; organic seal.
do_lines.wild_rice: “Wild rice” is the sole ingredient; no blend with white rice.
do_lines.beans_dried_vs_canned: Dry bag lists beans alone; canned label states a BPA-free lining.
do_lines.specialty_flours: One flour named in the ingredient list; organic printed on the bag.
do_lines.label_multigrain_vs_whole_grain: Read “100% whole grain” or “whole” before the grain name; “multigrain” alone fails.
do_lines.sprouted_grain_bread: “Sprouted” before each grain in the ingredient list, not flour first.
do_lines.sandwich_bread: Skip “enriched wheat flour”, sugar or soybean oil near the ingredient list’s top.
do_lines.gluten_free_bread: Skip unless the first ingredient names a flour with “whole” before it.
do_lines.bagels: Skip when ascorbic acid is listed; sourdough or sprouted on the bag passes.
do_lines.sugars: “Dehydrated cane juice” or organic cane sugar named, not “sugar” alone.
do_lines.maple_syrup: “Pure maple syrup” only; corn syrup in the ingredients means imitation.
do_lines.nuts_raw_vs_roasted: “Raw” printed on a sealed pack; coated or sugared nuts mean skip.
do_lines.nut_butter_ingredients: Ingredients: nuts, maybe salt; sugar, palm or “hydrogenated” words mean skip.
do_lines.seeds: Raw seeds sealed with a date; the seed is the lone ingredient.
do_lines.trail_mix: Sugar, chocolate or vegetable oil listed beside the nuts.
do_lines.pasta_sauce: Tomatoes first, oil named; no sugar or “natural flavors” listed.
do_lines.seaweed: Sea vegetable named alone; country of origin printed, and not China.
do_lines.hummus: Chickpeas, tahini, olive oil named; canola or soybean oil means skip.
do_lines.dried_herbs: One herb named on the jar; no blend listing citric acid or MSG.
do_lines.whole_spices: Whole seeds or sticks of one spice named; no “spices” blend.
do_lines.salt: Gray, pink, red or beige color; “iodized” on the label means skip.
do_lines.raw_cider_vinegar: “Raw” and “unfiltered” printed; cloudy strands of mother at the bottom.
do_lines.vinegar: “Distilled white vinegar” printed; apple cider, wine or balsamic named passes.
do_lines.ketchup_mustard: Tomatoes, vinegar, spices listed; no “natural flavors” entry.
do_lines.condiments: Soybean or canola oil named as the first oil on the label.
do_lines.crackers: Skip when white flour, hydrogenated oil or soy flour is listed.
do_lines.pretzels: Skip when refined white flour leads the ingredient list.
do_lines.rice_cakes_puffed_grains: Puffed grain with flavor coating, “natural flavor” or syrup in ingredients.
do_lines.kombucha: Organic on the label, in a glass bottle; black tea listed.
do_lines.coconut_water: Coconut water the sole ingredient; aseptic box means skip.
do_lines.beef_grassfed_vs_grainfed: AGA Grassfed seal; label reads 100% grass-fed and grass-finished.
do_lines.beef_cuts_basics: Whole cut in a sealed tray with AGA Grassfed seal and USDA Organic.
do_lines.ground_beef_lean_ratio: Ground beef pack naming grass-finished; ratio printed beside the AGA seal.
do_lines.hot_dogs: AGA seal on pack with a short ingredient list.
do_lines.lamb_goat: Lamb tray stamped AWA pasture; chops with pale pink fat.
do_lines.bison: Pack lists bison only; AGA Grassfed mark beside the cut.
do_lines.chicken_cuts_basics: Whole bird with AWA seal; skin cream-yellow, no basting solution listed.
do_lines.poultry_chicken_wings: Wings with skin intact, pack states organic and pasture-raised.
do_lines.rotisserie_chicken: Ingredients list only chicken and salt; organic seal on sticker.
do_lines.turkey_whole: Tag reads not basted; USDA Organic, Certified Humane Pasture Raised.
do_lines.ground_turkey: Pack states thigh and breast meat only, organic seal.
do_lines.poultry_duck: Whole duck with skin on and AWA or organic seal.
do_lines.pork_cuts_and_enhanced: Chop pack without added solution; AWA or Certified Humane pasture seal.
do_lines.salmon_wild_vs_farmed: Label says wild Alaskan; sockeye flesh deep red.
do_lines.label_wild_vs_farm_raised: Tag spells wild or farm-raised plus country and catch method.
do_lines.farmed_fish_by_species: ASC logo on pack when fish is farmed.
do_lines.shrimp_imported_vs_domestic: Bag names Gulf or US wild shrimp, shell on, no additives.
do_lines.white_fish: Pacific cod fillet, grey-brown skin side, species named on tag.
do_lines.seafood_fresh_sardines_mackerel: Mackerel with vivid stripes still bright; sardines with shiny skin.
do_lines.lobster: Live lobster moving its claws; frozen tails hard with no ice glaze.
do_lines.smoked_salmon: Label says wild or farm-raised, with origin; sold chilled.
do_lines.seafood_counter: Whole fish on ice with clear eyes and species sign.
do_lines.whole_vs_reduced_fat_milk: Read whole fat; skip milk stamped “ultra-pasteurized” near the date.
do_lines.oats_steelcut_rolled_instant: Read whole grain oats; skip instant packets listing flavor or sugar.
do_lines.cornmeal_polenta_grits: Check the USDA Organic seal; skip “degerminated” cornmeal.
do_lines.flour_basics: Read “whole wheat” on the bag; skip “bleached” or “enriched” flour.
do_lines.sourdough: Read “sourdough” and find a starter or culture in the ingredients.
do_lines.honey_adulteration: Look for “raw” and “unfiltered” honey, cloudy with pollen rather than clear.
do_lines.snack_bars: Skip bars listing brown rice syrup, agave or soy protein isolate.
do_lines.snacks: Read potatoes or corn, olive or coconut oil, salt; nothing else.
